The study investigates acute post-activation performance enhancement (PAPE) via contrasting high-load (HLBP) and low-load (BMT) conditioning activities. Using a crossover design, 28 trained males underwent three conditions: HLBP at 90% 1RM, BMT at 5% 1RM, and an active control. Confirmatory outcomes include PPO, APO, and PV measured at baseline, 5 min, and 10 min post-conditioning. Significant Condition × Time interactions were found for PPO and PV at 5 min, indicating differential temporal responses. However, no significant differences emerged at 10 min, and APO showed no change. Within HLBP, PPO and PV decreased at 5 min, partially recovering at 10 min, while BMT and CC showed no significant deviations from baseline. Contrary to hypotheses, HLBP did not outperform BMT, with the opposite trend observed at 5 min. This suggests that fatigue from HLBP outweighs any potential potentiation from BMT. The findings imply that neither conditioning activity produces meaningful PAPE under these protocols, likely due to the high-intensity fatigue induced by two sets of HLBP.
